body: President Zelensky says Starlink speeds in Ukraine are back to normal after more than a week of problems.
He also says Ukraine is ready for a three-way meeting with the US and Russia next month in Abu Dhabi.
The fighting goes on. A Ukrainian strike in Russia's Oryol region killed three people, the local governor said.
stories.headline: Ukraine's internet is back, and it says yes to peace talks
stories.joke: Starlink got fixed in a week. Your home broadband complaint is on day 40.
stories.statLabel: peace talks offered for next month
stories.vc: Satellite internet is now war infrastructure. Space and defence tech will keep pulling big money.

body: US President Donald Trump raised the idea of new military strikes on Iran on Friday.
He claimed the US could take all of Iran's oil, or even take over the whole country.
Any war talk near the Gulf pushes oil prices up. India imports most of its oil, so it feels this fast.
stories.headline: Trump talks about new strikes on Iran, and oil gets jumpy
stories.joke: Somewhere a petrol pump owner just bought a new pencil to update the price board.
stories.vc: Oil shocks hit India's markets first (see the Sensex card). Energy-saving and EV startups look smarter every time oil gets scary.

body: North Korea's leader Kim Jong Un is in China, South Korea's government said on Saturday.
It is his first trip there in a year.
China is North Korea's most important friend and trading partner, so these visits usually mean big talks on trade and security.
stories.headline: Kim Jong Un drops in on China
stories.joke: He usually travels by armoured train. Even his commute has a bigger budget than most seed rounds.
stories.vc: Asian politics move supply chains. Price in Korea and China risk when you look at any hardware startup.

body: Shops in Lyon and Orléans put up barriers, and luxury stores covered their windows ahead of fresh protests.
The mood is tense. On Friday a man was killed in a shooting near Paris that President Macron called a racist terror attack.
The victim was an amateur mixed martial arts fighter, his club said.
stories.headline: France boards up its shops before more protests
stories.vc: Street unrest is now a normal line in European deal risk. It also slows retail and tourism businesses there.

body: A strong typhoon called Champi hit Taiwan with giant waves and heavy winds.
More than 500 people were hurt and at least one person died.
Schools closed and travel across the island was thrown into chaos.
stories.headline: Typhoon Champi slams Taiwan
stories.vc: Taiwan makes most of the world's advanced chips. Every big storm there is a quiet stress test for global tech supply.

body: India's stock markets ended a two-week rally.
Two things pushed them down: an oil price shock and foreign investors selling Indian shares.
When foreign funds sell and oil rises at the same time, Indian markets and the rupee usually feel it together.
stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty stop their winning run
stories.joke: Dalal Street saw the oil price, said 'aiyyo', and left the party early.
stories.vc: When foreign money leaves public markets, late-stage startup funding in India often slows too. Valuations can get cheaper.

body: Kotak Mahindra Bank made a ₹5,645 crore profit in the July to September quarter.
That is 26% more than the same quarter last year.
Banks are a mirror of the economy. Big bank profits usually mean people and companies are borrowing and paying back.
stories.headline: Kotak Bank's profit jumps 26%
stories.joke: Record profits. Still charging you a fee for having 'low balance'.
stories.vc: Healthy banks lend to small businesses, and those businesses are the customers for most Indian fintech and SaaS.

body: Flipkart is testing a food delivery service called 'Eat-in by Minutes' with over 8,000 of its own employees in Bengaluru.
It could open to the public by the end of October, then grow to five or six cities by the end of the year.
It takes on Zomato and Swiggy, who share most of the market today.
stories.headline: Flipkart wants to deliver your dinner
stories.joke: Finally, a third app to blame when the biryani arrives cold.
stories.vc: Flipkart is reusing its quick-commerce delivery fleet. Giants enter new markets cheaply by reusing what they already own; startups need a sharper edge than that.

body: Market regulator SEBI ordered Avadhut Sathe Trading Academy to refund ₹546 crore.
It also put an ₹11.5 crore penalty on the academy.
Simple rule for everyone: before paying for stock tips or a trading course, check that the seller is SEBI-registered.
stories.headline: SEBI tells a trading academy to pay back ₹546 crore
stories.joke: Turns out the most profitable trade was selling the course.
stories.vc: Finfluencer money is easy until the regulator arrives. Back founders who build compliance in from day one.

body: Tamil Nadu has cut its VAT on aviation fuel at Chennai Airport from 29% to 16%.
At the state's other airports it drops to just 1%, said Air India, which thanked Chief Minister Vijay.
Fuel is one of an airline's biggest costs, so this can mean more flights from the state and maybe cheaper tickets.
stories.headline: Tamil Nadu cuts its tax on jet fuel
stories.joke: Chennai flights may get cheaper. The ₹300 airport filter coffee will not.
stories.vc: States now compete for airlines with tax cuts. Policy shifts like this open room for regional aviation and travel startups.

body: The FT's Lex column argues Indonesia's stock market is dysfunctional but still investable.
Timing is spicy: protests over economic policy and forest-fire smoke have spread to six Indonesian cities.
Lex also warned this earnings season that what CEOs promise about the future matters more than what they already did.
stories.headline: Lex: Indonesia is messy, but not a no-go
stories.joke: Translation: the house is a bit on fire, but the price is excellent.
stories.vc: Great deals hide in markets everyone calls 'broken'. Your job is telling messy from hopeless.

body: Tenstorrent, the AI chip company run by famous chip designer Jim Keller, raised $1.5 billion.
Its value more than doubled to $6.2 billion. Earlier this year Intel and Qualcomm showed interest in buying it, with offers reported up to $5 billion.
It said no and raised more money instead. It even has an office in Bangalore.
stories.headline: Chip startup Tenstorrent raises $1.5 billion
stories.joke: Saying no to $5 billion takes confidence. Most of us can't say no to a Swiggy coupon.
stories.vc: Rejecting a buyout is a bet on yourself. Investors paid up because buyers want cheaper, open alternatives to Nvidia.

body: Inspired Capital closed a $450 million fourth fund, betting on New York instead of Silicon Valley.
Andreessen Horowitz renamed its crypto arm 'a16z Frontier' as blockchain investing falls out of fashion.
Legal AI startup Legora raised $550 million at an $8.8 billion value.
stories.headline: New funds and a crypto rebrand: follow the VC money
stories.joke: Crypto didn't die. It just updated its LinkedIn headline.
stories.vc: Watch what funds rename and where they raise. When a16z drops 'crypto' from a name, the money already moved.

body: Meta released a new open-source AI model and is partnering with Apple so you can run it on your own device.
Ben Thompson also looked at Netflix's earnings and asked: is Netflix a business or a franchise?
Fun fact: Stratechery just took its first ever sponsor, Stripe.
stories.headline: Rivals Apple and Meta team up on AI
stories.joke: They fought for years over privacy. Now they share a brain. Love is real.
stories.vc: Frenemy deals show who owns which moat: Apple owns the device, Meta owns the model. Ask every startup which layer it owns.

body: This week's cover story is about the agony of liberal Europe.
Today's news backs it up: French shops boarding up, a Czech coalition rushing a media overhaul in an overnight vote, and fights in Albania's parliament.
Your one piece for today: read the cover Leader, then one Science & Technology story.
stories.headline: The Economist: liberal Europe is hurting
stories.joke: Europe: great cheese, great trains, slightly on fire.
stories.vc: When Europe gets unstable, its talent and capital look elsewhere. Make sure Bangalore is on that list.
